claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy films are ordered, single-phase, and hexagonal.
Low-fluence 30–50 keV He+ irradiation introduces point defects in the alloy films.
Low-fluence 30–50 keV He+ irradiation introduces dislocation loops in the alloy films.
The irradiation-induced defect density can be systematically controlled through irradiation dose.
A low-dose irradiation window exists in which defects can be introduced without amorphization or mechanical degradation.
Irradiation-induced point defects and dislocation loops act as heterogeneous nucleation sites during the magnetostructural transition.
The irradiation-induced defects lower the nucleation energy barrier for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Lowering the nucleation barrier makes the magnetostructural transition more gradual.
Making the transition more gradual broadens and smooths the magnetocaloric response.
Defect-mediated modification of the transition reduces magnetic hysteresis during low-applied-field cycling.
Irradiated samples will have a lower peak entropy change than the as-deposited baseline.
Irradiated samples will exhibit significantly less hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
The non-irradiated as-deposited films display a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The non-irradiated as-deposited films display high hysteresis.
The non-irradiated as-deposited films have limited heat-exchange performance.
Below the effective irradiation window, the dose will be insufficient to generate the defect density needed to modify the response.
Above the effective irradiation window, irradiation can cause structural damage and behavior outside the predicted trend.
The predicted effects are restricted to non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys retaining the ordered hexagonal phase.
